name: Natrunaiyappar Temple, Tirunanipalli (Ponsei)
deity: Shiva as Natrunaiyappar (the 'good companion'), with the goddess Malayaan Madanthai
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Ponsei, bearing the Tevaram name Tirunanipalli, near Sembanarkoil, honours Shiva as Natrunaiyappar — the 'good companion' — with the goddess Malayaan Madanthai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by all three great saints, Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar, it is revered as the birthplace of Bhagavati, the mother of Tirugnana Sambandar, and remembers how the child-saint's hymn is said to have turned its barren fields green.

sections.history: Ponsei, known in the Tevaram as Tirunanipalli, lies near Sembanarkoil in the Kaveri delta (sources place it in Mayiladuthurai district, older ones in Nagapattinam). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by all three of the great Tevaram saints — Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. The temple tradition holds Tirunanipalli to be the birthplace of Bhagavati, the devoted mother of the child-saint Tirugnana Sambandar, which gives the shrine a special tenderness in Shaiva memory. The stone temple belongs to the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Natrunaiyappar in the sanctum, with the goddess Malayaan Madanthai; a second form of the goddess, Parvatharaja Puthri, is also honoured here in the local tradition. A Nandi, the parivara devatas and a temple tank complete the simple plan. The temple is cared for at the scale of a village shrine of some antiquity.
sections.legends: The lord's name Natrunaiyappar — 'the father who is the good companion' — expresses his nearness to those who turn to him. By tradition the child Sambandar, passing this way, sang a pathikam here, and his hymn is said to have turned the barren, parched fields of Tirunanipalli into fertile land. The village is also remembered as the birthplace of Bhagavati Ammai, Sambandar's mother, binding the temple to the great saint's own story.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), the festival of Tirugnana Sambandar, and the regular Pradosha and Karthikai observances, at the quiet scale of a delta village. Devotees who follow the Paadal Petra trail and the trail of Sambandar's life include Tirunanipalli among their stops.
sections.experience: To come to Ponsei is to stand at a shrine woven into the life of the child-saint Sambandar. Before Natrunaiyappar, the 'good companion,' and Malayaan Madanthai, the pilgrim feels the gentle grace of a temple that remembers a hymn turning barren earth green — a small delta sanctuary rich in the memory of devotion.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Ponsei (Tirunanipalli) is about 4 km from Sembanarkoil and roughly 13 km from Mayiladuthurai, in the Kaveri delta. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis via Sembanarkoil to the village.
